UDP Broadcast Example

Send and receive UDP broadcast datagrams with gxSocket (DataReel 7.4).

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

Plain text. The datagrams are not encrypted or authenticated: anyone on the network can read them or send forged ones. Use this only on a trusted local network, for data that is not secret. Every other DataReel 7 network example uses TLS.

Based on the 2001 broadcast sender and receiver programs, on the DataReel 7 gxSocket datagram calls:

  • send: OpenDatagram(AF_INET), SO_BROADCAST with SetSockOpt(), then SendTo() a broadcast address: 255.255.255.255 (this network), a subnet's broadcast address such as 192.168.1.255, or 127.255.255.255 (this host only).
  • recv: OpenDatagram(AF_INET, port) binds the port on every address, then RecvFrom() with a timeout prints each datagram and its sender.

Broadcasts are IPv4 only (IPv6 uses multicast instead, see udp_multicast) and routers do not forward them, so they stay on the local network.

Running It

udp_broadcast send address port [--count N] [--interval ms] [text]
udp_broadcast recv port [--count N] [--timeout seconds]

recv exits 0 when N datagrams arrived and 1 when none came for the timeout (10 seconds by default). Start the receiver first.

Sample Output

$ udp_broadcast recv 24520 --count 3 &
receiving broadcasts on port 24520
$ udp_broadcast send 127.255.255.255 24520 --count 3 --interval 50 hello
sent "hello 1" to 127.255.255.255:24520
sent "hello 2" to 127.255.255.255:24520
sent "hello 3" to 127.255.255.255:24520
from 127.0.0.1:35730: hello 1
from 127.0.0.1:35730: hello 2
from 127.0.0.1:35730: hello 3
3 datagrams received

Source

examples/diagnostics/udp_broadcast.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as udp_broadcast and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.

Send and receive UDP broadcast datagrams with gxSocket (OpenDatagram,
SendTo, RecvFrom). Based on the 2001 broadcast sender and receiver
programs.

PLAIN TEXT: datagrams are not encrypted or authenticated and anyone
on the network can read or forge them. Use broadcasts only on a
trusted local network, for data that is not secret.

Usage: udp_broadcast send address port [--count N] [--interval ms]
                     [text]
       udp_broadcast recv port [--count N] [--timeout seconds]

  send  sends N datagrams ("text 1", "text 2", ...) to the address,
        such as 255.255.255.255, a subnet's broadcast address
        (192.168.1.255) or 127.255.255.255 on this host
  recv  prints each datagram and its sender until N arrived (exit 0)
        or no datagram came for the timeout (exit 1)

#include "gxdlcode.h"

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>
#include "gxsocket.h"

using namespace datareel;

static int usage(const char *prog)
{
  std::cerr << "Usage: " << prog << " send address port [--count N] [--interval ms] [text]\n"
            << "       " << prog << " recv port [--count N] [--timeout seconds]\n";
  return 1;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  if(argc < 3) return usage(argv[0]);
  std::string mode = argv[1];
  int count = 5, interval_ms = 200, timeout = 10;
  std::string text = "broadcast";
  std::vector<std::string> pos;
  for(int i = 2; i < argc; i++) {
    std::string a = argv[i];
    if(a == "--count" && i + 1 < argc) count = std::atoi(argv[++i]);
    else if(a == "--interval" && i + 1 < argc) interval_ms = std::atoi(argv[++i]);
    else if(a == "--timeout" && i + 1 < argc) timeout = std::atoi(argv[++i]);
    else pos.push_back(a);
  }
  if(count < 1) count = 1;

  gxSocket s;
  if(mode == "send") {
    if(pos.size() < 2) return usage(argv[0]);
    if(pos.size() > 2) text = pos[2];
    std::vector<gxsAddress> to;
    if(gxsAddress::Resolve(pos[0], std::atoi(pos[1].c_str()), to, SOCK_DGRAM, AF_INET) != 0) {
      std::cerr << "Cannot resolve " << pos[0] << "\n";
      return 1;
    }
    if(s.OpenDatagram(AF_INET) != 0) {
      std::cerr << s.SocketExceptionMessage() << "\n";
      return 1;
    }
    int on = 1; // A broadcast address needs SO_BROADCAST
    if(s.SetSockOpt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST, &on, sizeof(on)) != 0) {
      std::cerr << "SO_BROADCAST: " << s.SocketExceptionMessage() << "\n";
      return 1;
    }
    for(int n = 1; n <= count; n++) {
      std::string msg = text + " " + std::to_string(n);
      if(s.SendTo(to[0], msg.data(), (int)msg.size()) < 0) {
        std::cerr << "Send to " << to[0].ToString() << ": " << s.SocketExceptionMessage() << "\n";
        return 1;
      }
      std::cout << "sent \"" << msg << "\" to " << to[0].ToString() << "\n";
      if(n < count) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(interval_ms));
    }
    return 0;
  }
  if(mode == "recv") {
    if(pos.empty()) return usage(argv[0]);
    if(s.OpenDatagram(AF_INET, std::atoi(pos[0].c_str())) != 0) {
      std::cerr << "Bind port " << pos[0] << ": " << s.SocketExceptionMessage() << "\n";
      return 1;
    }
    std::cout << "receiving broadcasts on port " << pos[0] << "\n" << std::flush;
    char buf[65536];
    for(int n = 0; n < count; n++) {
      gxsAddress from;
      int bytes = s.RecvFrom(from, buf, (int)sizeof(buf), timeout);
      if(bytes < 0) {
        std::cerr << "no datagram for " << timeout << " seconds (" << n << " of "
                  << count << " received)\n";
        return 1;
      }
      std::cout << "from " << from.ToString() << ": " << std::string(buf, bytes) << "\n" << std::flush;
    }
    std::cout << count << " datagrams received\n";
    return 0;
  }
  return usage(argv[0]);
}
